claim.text: Approximately 47.9 million people experienced food insecurity in 2024, and household food insecurity remained around 13.7% in the current brief.

outcome_artifact.source_unit: Statistical Supplement to Household Food Security in the United States in 2024, AP-126, Table S-11
outcome_artifact.population: U.S. households and persons in households represented by the December 2024 CPS Food Security Supplement
outcome_artifact.measure: household-reported receipt of free groceries and free meals from community food and nutrition assistance programs
uncertainty: Question wording changed in 2022, so free-grocery and free-meal estimates are not comparable with earlier pantry/kitchen series.
Address-based CPS sampling excludes people experiencing homelessness and may underrepresent tenuously housed people, especially for free-meal use.
The table measures household-reported receipt, not provider visits, meals served, capacity, wait time, cost, or revenue.
outcome_artifact.counterinterpretation: This is an official household-reported outcome context. It does not establish causality, provider capacity, market size, or independent confirmation of an IBIS claim.
outcome_artifact.rights_boundary: Retain normalized values, source locator, checksum, and attribution; do not redistribute the upstream PDF or reproduce its tables without exact-artifact rights review.

independent_publisher_challenge.method_and_dependence: Feeding America models local estimates using CPS-FSS, ACS, BLS/LAUS, and local food-price inputs; the national page is a modeled estimate, not a direct provider transaction or visit count.
comparability_limits: This publisher's modeled individual-level estimate is not directly comparable to USDA's household CPS-FSS receipt measures.
The 2026 release reports 2024 estimates and should not be treated as a contemporaneous 2026 outcome.
Food insecurity and food budget shortfall are demand-context measures, not provider capacity, visits, meals served, or revenue.

lineage_adjudication.reason: Feeding America is a distinct publisher, but its modeled estimate uses CPS-FSS, ACS, BLS/LAUS, and food-price inputs; the USDA artifact is also direct official context and FRAC may summarize it. Distinct publishers are not counted as independent models until source-level lineage and input overlap are signed off.
lineage_adjudication.outcome_linkage: household receipt of free groceries and free meals is a closer community-food-use outcome than food insecurity alone, but it still does not measure provider visits, capacity, wait time, cost, or revenue

required_next_steps: Confirm whether the FRAC record is a restatement of the USDA artifact and record the source lineage.
Acquire a direct community-food-service utilization or capacity outcome with a defined denominator.
Reconcile the outcome period, population, unit, uncertainty, and rights before any IBIS qualification.
boundary: This artifact documents one acquired official outcome context and its limits. It does not validate the IBIS claim, establish demand causality, prove independent confirmation, or authorize an internal company bridge.
